title: Favorite pieces and uncredited background use
summary: The Open Mind theme and television use of the records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you have some favorites among the pieces that you wrote for the band?

One of them was a piece for flute and piano that they used for a theme song for many years, a program called The Open Mind on NBC. I thought it would have changed my fortune a lot if they gave me credit for some of those things. They used to use Sauter-Finegan things all the time as background music, as dramatic underscoring for dramatic shows, without credit.
I didn't think that was right; I still don't think so.
Did you take them to court over it?
There's nothing you can do about it. If they use a record they're free to do that, so you couldn't. The only way you could do it would be through their good graces, which they did not have.

But it would have changed a lot of things for me had they done that because after Sauter-Finegan, that's really what I wanted to do, but I didn't know how to do it. I didn't arrive at it until Stan did it with Mickey One, but that stopped abruptly, so nothing came out of that. I guess the picture didn't do anything.
You always have to be involved with a hit, and the people want other hits.
